findings.title: SCAN.MATHBF now admits `\mathbf{1}` unconditionally, overriding the consumer's `notation.mathbf_allowed`, and the policy that forbade it was rewritten in the same change set
findings.before: `    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"]))` — and policy/latex-idiom.md at base: "Never the other, and never an upright `\mathbf` outside the admitted list."
findings.after: `    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}")` — and policy/latex-idiom.md at head adds: "`\mathbf{1}`, the indicator and identity of `RULE.TEX.MATHBB`, is admitted in every package whatever that list holds; it is not a package's to withhold."
findings.why_it_matters: SCAN.MATHBF is a `hard` scan: a hit is exit 1 from `gbg scan docs` and an `error()` from the `makedocs` wrapper. A consumer whose config says `mathbf_allowed = []` (a legal value — the schema's `strlist` has no minItems, and `["\\mathbf{1}"]` is only a *default*) previously had `\mathbf{1}` in a docstring or page refused by that hard scan; after this edit the same file passes clean, with no ledger entry, no exemption and no report line. The configuration key is now partly inert: emptying it, or listing other strings without this one, no longer forbids what it used to forbid. Two of the four science consumers are on `notation.vectors = "boldsymbol"` and their configs are frozen until their migration phase, so nobody will notice the key stopped meaning what it says. The self-certifying shape is what makes this a lane finding rather than a design note: the same commit that hardcoded the exception into the tool also rewrote the rendered policy paragraph and the schema description so that the new behaviour reads as the rule.
findings.description: The guard removed is the config-driven whitelist itself. At base the scan asked exactly one question — is this `\mathbf{…}` string in the list this package declared? — and the tool held no literal of its own. At head the tool injects `\mathbf{1}` into every consumer's allowed set before the test, so no package can refuse it. If a fleet-wide standing exception is genuinely intended, it belongs where the other non-configurable facts live (ARCHITECTURE §5.5's non-configurable set, or the schema's `const`/`minItems` so an author who empties the list is told), not as a silent `push!` that leaves the key looking configurable. Note also the direction of the invariant the package states for itself: "A consumer holds data; the tool holds behaviour... No package string... in a Workflow script, a catalogue file or a policy file" — a package-visible notation literal now lives in the tool's scan body. The narrower point stands regardless of that reading: input that was previously refused (a `\mathbf{1}` under a config that did not admit it) now yields a clean scan.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:4798-4813 `-    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"]))` / `+    allowed = Set(String.(cfg["notation"]["mathbf_allowed"])); push!(allowed, "\\mathbf{1}")`; diff.patch:2045-2051 policy/latex-idiom.md `-outside the admitted list.` / `+outside the admitted list. \`\\mathbf{1}\`, the indicator and identity of \`RULE.TEX.MATHBB\`, is admitted in`; diff.patch:2087-2094 schema/config.schema.json `+     "description": "...SCAN.MATHBF admits it whatever this list holds, so emptying the list does not forbid it"`. Current code confirms the membership test is exact: `m.match in allowed || push!(hits, ...)`.

findings.title: Scoped passes retire "every pass verifies every id", and the two mechanisms that decide re-verification silently exclude whole classes of finding
findings.before: `    findings = findings_of(dir)` in `pass_open`, and in `grade`: `inst = rec["instrument"]; findings = findings_of(dir); ledger = Ledger.read(cfg)` / `per_id = Dict{String,Any}(); dead = String[]; ...` — every banked id was re-verified by both verifiers on every pass, and every id's entry in every tally came from a verdict written for that pass.
findings.after: `    scope, prev_open, suspects, fixrange = pass_scope(cfg, dir, rec, k)` / `    findings = scope === nothing ? all_findings : [f for f in all_findings if f["id"] in scope || f["lane"] == "scans"]`, and in `grade`: `carried = Dict{String,Any}(String(i) => e for (i, e) in read_json(prevtally)["per_id"] if !(String(i) in scope))` / `per_id = copy(carried); ...`
findings.why_it_matters: A closed finding is now re-verified only if `any(x -> x in touched, finding_files(root, f))` holds, and three separate filters can make that false for a finding that did regress: (1) `finding_files` keeps a location token only when `isfile(joinpath(root, f))`, so a location that names no resolvable repo path — a bare basename such as `GBGCodingTools.jl:15`, a docstring-unit key such as `Config.jl :: read`, a heading reference — yields `[]`, and an id whose locations are all of that kind can never become a suspect and is skipped outright by `unswept` (`isempty(named) && continue`); (2) the same `isfile` filter drops a path the fix pass DELETED or RENAMED, which is precisely the edit most likely to break a closed finding's fix; (3) `touched` is `Git.changed_paths(root, range, Preflight.covered_paths(cfg))`, and `covered_paths` is only `["src","test","ext","docs","Project.toml"]` plus `[paths]` — a regression in `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or any tracked file outside that set is invisible to the suspect test. In each case the id keeps, verbatim, the `act`/`state`/`closed_by` entry a previous pass wrote, and pass k's `tally.json` asserts verdicts nobody re-checked at pass k. `plateau.passes_flat` then compares `length(open_ids)` across passes that verified different sets, and `totals`/`adjudicated_share` are computed over `all_findings` while `per_id` mixes fresh and carried entries.
findings.description: The cost argument for scoping is real and is recorded (ARCHITECTURE §6.2 step 7: "the rc.1 round verified 56 findings ten times over where 90 verifications were owed"). What is not justified is the fail-open shape of the two predicates that implement it. Both `unswept` and `pass_scope` treat "I could not resolve a file for this finding" as "nothing to check", when the safe reading of an unresolvable location is the opposite: verify it. A minimal repair is to keep an id in scope whenever `finding_files` comes back empty, and to compute `touched` over the whole tree (or at least to include a named path that no longer exists as touched) rather than over `covered_paths`. Note the quantifier trap the brief names: none of this shows up as "input that used to work now behaves differently" — the affected findings are ones the previous pass CLOSED, so no other lane's question reaches them.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:3388-3397 `+        for m in eachmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./\\-]*\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+", String(l))` / `+            isfile(joinpath(root, f)) && !(f in out) && push!(out, f)`; diff.patch:3424-3430 `+    touched = Set(Git.changed_paths(root, range, Preflight.covered_paths(cfg)))` / `+        any(x -> x in touched, finding_files(root, f)) && push!(suspects, id)`; diff.patch:3456-3458 `+        (get(f, "seeded", false) || f["lane"] == "scans") && continue` / `+        named = finding_files(root, f)` / `+        isempty(named) && continue`; diff.patch:3570-3576 `+    per_id = copy(carried); dead = String[]; ...`. `src/CLI/Preflight.jl:400`: `covered_paths(cfg) = unique(vcat(["src", "test", "ext", "docs", "Project.toml"], String.(values(cfg["paths"]))))`.

findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM's new element-type exemption fires on the keyword's NAME alone, so a docstring documenting neither of its arguments now passes a hard scan
findings.after: `        eltype_kw = length(kw) == 1 && occursin(r"^(T|eltype|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*_type)$", first(kw))` / `        wants_bullets = length(pos) + length(kw) >= Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD ||` / `                        (!isempty(kw) && !(eltype_kw && length(pos) + length(kw) < Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD))`
findings.why_it_matters: Take `f(x; T = Float64)` with a docstring that documents nothing about its arguments — no `The arguments are:` bullets and no `The arguments are \`…\`` prose. With `ARGS_THRESHOLD = 3`: base computed `wants_bullets = (2 >= 3) || !isempty(["T"]) = true`, `bulleted = false`, and pushed the hard hit "`f` takes 1 positional and 1 keyword argument(s): the bulleted `The arguments are:` form, not prose". Head computes `eltype_kw = true`, so `wants_bullets = (2 >= 3) || (true && !(true && 2 < 3)) = false`; `bulleted` and `prosed` are both false, no branch fires, and the docstring is clean. RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM's exemption is "a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause" — a permission granted to a docstring that HAS the prose clause. The scan checks neither that the prose clause exists nor that the keyword is an element type; it matches a name against `^(T|eltype|.*_type)$`, which also admits keywords like `arg_type`, `hit_type` or `round_type` that carry no element semantics at all. The rule's own gate (any keyword forces the argument to be documented somehow) is therefore removed for a class the scan cannot identify.
findings.description: The exemption itself is warranted — `git show <base>:policy/docs-rubric.md` shows the element-type clause already in RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM at base, so this is not a rule invented to fit the code. The implementation is wider than the rule in the direction that fails silently: it exempts on a name pattern instead of on the presence of the prose binding the rule requires. Gating `eltype_kw` on `prosed` (i.e. exempt only when the docstring actually binds the arguments in running prose) would restore the rule's meaning and cost nothing. The same edit is also narrower than the rule in the loud direction, which is worth stating because it is the same line: for a two-argument docstring with a `T` keyword written in bullets — clean at base, since `wants_bullets` was true — head now takes the `!wants_bullets && bulleted` branch and hits with "bind them in running prose, not bullets", converting the rule's permission into an obligation.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:4754-4761 `-        wants_bullets = length(pos) + length(kw) >= Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD || !isempty(kw)` / `+        eltype_kw = length(kw) == 1 && occursin(r"^(T|eltype|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*_type)$", first(kw))` / `+        wants_bullets = ... || (!isempty(kw) && !(eltype_kw && length(pos) + length(kw) < Reflection.ARGS_THRESHOLD))`. `src/Reflection.jl:29`: `const ARGS_THRESHOLD = 3`. Base rule text (`git show <base>:policy/docs-rubric.md`, RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM): "Exempt: ... and a single element-type keyword bound in one prose clause."

findings.title: RULE.DOC.SHAPE's statement was weakened to match what the scan already did, while the policy paragraph the consumers read was left saying the stronger thing
findings.before: RULES.toml: `statement = "A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always; no unit grows past its baseline; ..."`; src/Scans/prose_shape.jl: `# Caps bind ALWAYS (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions; IT's lesson: a cap that applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming).`; ARCHITECTURE §12.B: `caps 120 words / 3 admonitions always`
findings.after: RULES.toml: `statement = "...at most 3 admonitions; no unit grows past its baseline, and a page unit already baselined is held by that ratchet alone; ..."`; src/Scans/prose_shape.jl: `# Caps ... bind on every docstring and every NEW page unit; a page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone, the one place IT's lesson ... is traded for an append-only log.`; ARCHITECTURE §12.B: `caps ... on every docstring and every NEW page unit, a baselined page unit held by the ratchet alone`
findings.why_it_matters: No line of `register_scan!("SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE", ...)` changed in this window — the `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing` guard and its inner comment ("a baselined page section is held by the ratchet alone") are identical at base and head. So the change set did not fix the divergence between the stated rule and the enforced one; it moved the stated rule down to the enforced one. RULES.toml's `statement` is the line the instruments cite and the panel hats are handed, so the class "a baselined page section whose longest paragraph is over 120 words" has gone from a rule violation a reviewer could name to a documented allowance. Meanwhile `policy/docs-rubric.md`'s own paragraph — the text `gbg sync` renders into every consumer's `.gbg/policy/` — was NOT changed, so the rendered rulebook and the rule index now say different things about the same id.
findings.description: This is the "contract rewritten to match the behaviour" shape with the behaviour standing still. The defensible options were: change the code so a baselined page unit is still capped (which is what "always" promised and what IT's own recorded lesson argues for), or, if the trade is deliberate, change all three surfaces together and say so in `CHANGELOG.md` as a policy relaxation. What was done instead relaxes the rule index and ARCHITECTURE while leaving the rendered policy paragraph stronger, so a consumer reading `.gbg/policy/docs-rubric.md` and a hat reading the RULES.toml statement are now enforcing different rules. Flagged as minor rather than major only because the underlying under-enforcement pre-dates this window; the relaxation of the written norm is inside it.
findings.evidence: `git diff <base>..<head> -- policy/RULES.toml`: `-statement = "A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always; no unit grows past its baseline; ..."` / `+statement = "A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions; no unit grows past its baseline, and a page unit already baselined is held by that ratchet alone; ..."`. diff.patch:4815-4831 shows src/Scans/prose_shape.jl's hunk header `@@ -1,8 +1,9 @@` — comment lines only. Current code, unchanged: `        if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing`. `policy/docs-rubric.md:206-210` is absent from the diff.

findings.title: The round-lifecycle test no longer exercises the default `pass open` path — the same commit that added the sweep refusal re-baselined the assertion that used to cover it
findings.after: `        @test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; io = devnull) == 2` / `        @test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; sweep_ok = true, io) == 0`
findings.why_it_matters: The lifecycle test is the only place `pass_open` is driven end to end against a real round directory, and after this edit every remaining assertion downstream of it — the `verify-act.js`/`verify-state.js` render, `pass.toml`, the verdict round-trip, `grade` — runs only under `sweep_ok = true`, the override branch. The default branch that a session will actually take (`gbg round pass open <round>` with no flag, after a real fix pass) is now asserted only to return 2. A regression in the non-override path — the `scope`/`expected` computation, the lane filter `get(expected_state, r["key"], 0) > 0 || r["key"] == "scans"`, the `scope` key written into `pass.toml` — would leave every assertion in this file green.
findings.description: The re-baseline itself is honest: the comment added beside it says plainly that "this lifecycle plants verdicts instead of fixing, so it says so rather than pretending otherwise", and the new `@testset "a pass verifies what is open, and refuses an unswept fix"` does test `unswept`, `finding_files` and `pass_scope` as units. What is missing is a lifecycle run through the default path — a fixture round whose fix pass actually touches the files its findings name, so `pass_open` returns 0 without `sweep_ok`. Without it, the flag that exists for the exceptional case is the only case the integration test covers, and the guard added in this commit is the reason. This is the oracle-inside-the-change-set shape: the test that would have caught a default-path regression was edited by the commit that introduced the branch.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:5349-5353 `-        @test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; io) == 0` / `+        # the sweep check refuses a pass whose fix touched none of what the open findings name; this` / `+        # lifecycle plants verdicts instead of fixing, so it says so rather than pretending otherwise` / `+        @test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; io = devnull) == 2` / `+        @test G.Passes.pass_open(cfg, round; sweep_ok = true, io) == 0`.

findings.title: `TestHarness.resolve_function` now prefers a package binding over the Base generic it extends, which can make `module_method_count` undercount methods a consumer's frozen parity baseline was written to cover
findings.before: `    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))`
findings.after: `    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))`
findings.why_it_matters: `module_method_count` sums `count(m -> m.module === mod, methods(f))` over every name `Reflection.all_package_functions` yields. When a package extends a Base generic (`show`, `size`, `length`, `read`) AND also has a same-named binding of its own inside one of its submodules, the resolved `f` changes from the Base generic — whose method table contains the package's added methods — to the package's own function, whose table does not. The `[module]` totals in a consumer's frozen `test/method_parity_baseline.toml` were recorded under the old resolution; under the new one those methods stop being counted, so a method later added to the extended Base generic no longer moves the total the baseline asserts. The parity gate's coverage narrows silently, in the direction this lane watches.
findings.description: The stated motive ("a package function always wins its own name") is reasonable and the docstring names three examples in this very package, but the change is to a public harness engine that this repository does not exercise: there is no `test/method_parity.jl` and no `method_parity_baseline.toml` under `test/`, and the tool's declared deviations put the allocation and traffic contracts out of scope here. Its only consumers are the four science packages, whose frozen baselines were not and could not be regenerated in this change set. That leaves a computed count altered with no oracle anywhere in the tree, and the first evidence either way will be a consumer's `Pkg.test()` after the next `gbg bump`. Confidence is medium, not high, because the practical reach depends on whether `isdefined(pkg, name)` already resolved a Base-exported name at the umbrella — in which case the reorder is inert for exported generics and bites only for the shadowed submodule case described above.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:4960-4961 `-    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` / `+    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))`; diff.patch:4953-4955 the added rationale `- \`externals\` — the external modules whose generics the package extends, searched LAST so a package function always wins its own name (\`Config.read\`, \`Git.run\` and \`Scan.report\` all share one with a \`Base\` export, and Base ahead of them handed the caller the wrong generic).` `ls test/` shows no `method_parity.jl` and no baseline TOML; the diffstat lists no baseline file.

findings.title: `CFG.SURFACES` no longer requires `docs/make.jl` to exist; the guard survives only because `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` still hardcodes the path
findings.before: `    isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")`
findings.after: `    scripts = [String(m.match) for m in eachmatch(r"[^\s\"']+\.jl", cfg["package"]["docs_build"])]` / `    isempty(scripts) && push!(errs, "package.docs_build: names no .jl script to run")` / `    for s in scripts` / `        isfile(joinpath(root, s)) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: $(repr(s)) does not exist")` / `    end`
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer whose `docs_build` is, say, `julia --project=docs docs/site.jl` and which has no `docs/make.jl` at all now passes `CFG.SURFACES` and `Config.read(check = true)`, where at base it failed. That matters for the paths that call `Config.read`/`check_paths` without a doctor run — the Step-0 scratch configs and `Config.parse` — and it means the two checks now disagree about the same tree.
findings.description: The fix itself is right and the base text was the defect: checking a fixed path while ignoring the script the command actually runs meant the file that runs went unchecked. The residue is that the unconditional `docs/make.jl` requirement was dropped from `CFG.SURFACES` while `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` still demands `docs/make.jl` by name (`isfile(p) || return fail("WIRE.MAKEDOCS", "docs/make.jl absent")`), so the loosening is fully shadowed for any real consumer: `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` is in `QUICK` and in `NON_EXEMPTABLE`. Hence nit, not minor. Worth a line only so that a later relaxation of `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` — which the new `CFG.SURFACES` text invites, since it now speaks of "every `.jl` script the `docs_build` command names" — is not made on the assumption that `CFG.SURFACES` is still holding that requirement.
findings.evidence: diff.patch:2999-3006 `-    isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")` / `+    scripts = [String(m.match) for m in eachmatch(r"[^\s\"']+\.jl", cfg["package"]["docs_build"])]` ...; `src/CLI/Doctor.jl:377-378`: `    p = joinpath(ctx.root, "docs", "make.jl")` / `    isfile(p) || return fail("WIRE.MAKEDOCS", "docs/make.jl absent")`; `src/CLI/Doctor.jl:40-44` show `WIRE.` in both `NON_EXEMPTABLE` and `QUICK`.
